argument_summary: The admissible record does not support clean compliance on a rollout-controls-alone theory, but it does support a narrower position: certification is defensible only on a constrained basis that treats aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, 7% rollout, rollback, and monitoring as mitigation context while expressly conceding that the telehealth discharge planning segment remains exposed and below target. Under the policy record, that exposure creates a disclosure condition, not a pre-launch resolution condition. The audit concern is therefore overstated to the extent it treats the current packet as claiming rollout controls eliminate the weakness. The defensible packet is certification with an explicit model-card limitation for the named launch use case and without any claim that the incomplete risk-acceptance draft satisfies policy.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not required to manage the remaining uncertainty on this record because the weakness is already bounded in scope, the rollout is limited to 7%, rollback exists, aggregate readiness passed, and rehearsal recorded no severity-one incidents. Those facts do not erase the disclosure obligation, but they do reduce the case for treating the certification request as needing further escalation if the auditor can record the limitation as a binding caveat rather than block the packet outright.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy evidence says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed, unless the use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. The admissible record shows no exclusion and no approved risk acceptance. It also shows a separate policy requirement that material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On that record, the supportable policy position is not unconditional compliance; it is caveated compliance only if certification is grounded in explicit disclosure of the telehealth discharge planning limitation and not in the claim that rollout controls alone satisfy the policy predicate.
concessions: The telehealth discharge planning segment remains below target on post-visit instruction summarization and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The random clinic gate does not exclude the affected telehealth discharge planning segment.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has no approver, and does not address the telehealth discharge planning exposure.
The current admissible record does not support a claim that rollout controls alone satisfy policy.
The current admissible record does not prove clean compliance absent explicit disclosure of the limitation.
